paper.citation: Benkeser, D., Carone, M., van der Laan, M. J. and Gilbert, P. B. (2017). Doubly robust nonparametric inference on the average treatment effect. Biometrika 104(4), 863–880. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asx053.
paper.source_locator: Section 5.1, 'Data-generating mechanism and crossvalidation set-up'; PMC full-text HTML lines 301–304; printed journal pages approximately 870–871. Equations are unnumbered in the prose. PDF page number not visually verified in this run. Exact expressions transcribed from PMC full-text text rendering.

mechanism.name: Binary-outcome observational ATE design with nonlinear treatment and outcome regressions

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; within individual, A depends on W and Y depends on (A,W); W1 and W2 are mutually independent as specified in Section 5.1.

assumptions: Consistency and well-defined binary treatment interventions.
Conditional exchangeability: (Y(0),Y(1)) independent of A given W.
Positivity: 0 < P(A=1|W=w) < 1 on the support of W; here the expit probability is strictly between zero and one for every finite w in the bounded support.
Independent sampling of individuals; no interference.

properties.notes: Two baseline covariates only, so not high-dimensional. The explicit interaction is W1*W2 in both logit treatment and logit outcome regressions. Nonlinearity is the expit/logistic link; outcome is binary.

estimand.name: ATE = E[Y(1)-Y(0)]
estimand.definition: Population risk difference under interventions setting A=1 versus A=0, averaged over the source covariate distribution W=(W1,W2).

parameters.description: Section 5.1 source DGP; nuisance-estimation scenarios I/II/III change which nuisance estimator is consistent, not the underlying data-generating law.

truth.expression: Population risk difference under interventions setting A=1 versus A=0, averaged over the source covariate distribution W=(W1,W2).
truth.derivation: Integrate Qbar(1,w)-Qbar(0,w) over W1~Uniform(-2,2) and W2~Bernoulli(1/2), using Gauss-Legendre quadrature; independently verify with composite Simpson integration.
